body: @domenic can you help me locate the tests for these features? (And maybe help tweak them.)

Thanks very much for taking this on.

Any particular reason this removes the credentials mode feature from the `Worker` constructor instead of just changing the default? That removes two abilities in particular:

- The ability to set the credentials mode to omit. (Not present in type=module after this change.)
- The ability to set the credentials mode to include for imports. (Which you can do with type=module via crossorigin=use-credentials)

All else being equal I'd rather keep that option...

/cc @nhiroki @mattto for tracking as they are implementing currently.

Tests might be best uncovered by someone actually implementing this (perhaps @domfarolino or @hiroshige-g are interested) and seeing what breaks. The tests are all in https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-script-element/module . The crossorigin-* ones are the only ones that seem relevant from first scan...

I don't think we should offer the ability to use credentials mode "omit" outside `fetch()` until we tackle it more generally (see #2614). We could keep the ability to use "include" with a more restricted enum I suppose. It wasn't entirely clear to me if v1 needed that as we don't really have use cases other than the worry about connection sharing in non-Firefox browsers.

I guess we can remove it, I just worry that people are going to be complaining and then we'll just add everything back.

I'm not sure this would be blocked on #2614 since solving omit for the markup use case is pretty different from solving it for the API use case. We already have API precedent with fetch().

The API argument is somewhat interesting, but we don't have any other API offer this functionality today, which is why I'm hesitant (but also fine with adding it if folks will implement it). E.g., `EventSource` does not.

Does service workers require changes here?

cc @jungkees @jakearchibald

Worklets have [```credentials``` option that defaults to ```omit```](https://drafts.css-houdini.org/worklets/#worklet-section) and [WPTs for the option](https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/blob/master/worklets/resources/credentials-tests.js).

Modules workers don't have WPTs for the ```credentials``` option yet.

Filed an issue in the chromium bug tracker: https://crbug.com/838540
cc @wanderview @jonco3

Reg: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/3656#issuecomment-385663659

> Worklets have credentials option that defaults to omit and WPTs for the option.

I changed the Worklet spec and WPTs (https://github.com/w3c/css-houdini-drafts/issues/756)

> Modules workers don't have WPTs for the credentials option yet.

I added WPTs for the ```credentials``` param of WorkerOptions for dedicated workers based on the current spec (i.e., ```omit``` is the default value) (https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/commit/d9a5af281709894851abcaff5c3af967dc0b474e). I'll update the tests based on the conclusion of this PR.
Okay, I guess I should bring the `credentials` member back in this PR and then we can proceed? @domenic?
That would work great for me; matching worklets makes a lot of sense.
Updated the commit as well as its description.
@domenic given that you haven't replied to the concerns raised in that issue as well as the concerns raised in #3109 for many months that's rather frustrating.
I've replied; I think we just have different views on the relative importance of different issues, and the path forward.

Hmm..., this is a tough topic. I'm still weighing up the options. Cross-origin worker looks appealing. It allows to directly load library workers hosted on CDNs without a same-origin skeleton script. On the other hand, it introduces complication around Clients API, Service Worker interception, security features, etc. Maybe I'm slightly leaning to no support of the cross-origin worker for now because of the complication.

Regarding the cumbersome skeleton script, JS Blocks could mitigate it like this, I'm not sure how to determine a controller service worker in this case though.

```js
const block = { import "https://other.example.com/worker-lib.js"; };
const worker = new worker(block, { type: 'module' });
```

Or, LAPIs could provide worker libraries commonly used??

Yeah, no support for now seems reasonable. We could indeed contemplate better APIs in the future, e.g. ones that create a wrapper for you automatically. Although that feels pretty similar to what's already in the spec, just phrased differently...

Anyway, if you're OK removing support for cross-origin workers for now, then we can move ahead with this. We still need tests, including for the change to script type=module, but hopefully you (or @hiroshige-g?) can help us with that.
Will have time to check this out in detail tonight if it's possible to hold out on merging until then!

Removing cross-origin worker support for now LGTM. I'll update the tests/implementation for dedicated workers. Specifically, workers/modules/dedicated-worker-options-credentials.html. We don't have tests for shared workers and service workers yet because there're no module implementation for them. I'll add the tests for them when starting implementation.

Seems that all of the changes introduced by this PR at this point can be summarized as following:
 1. Change [module script credentials mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#module-script-credentials-mode) to no longer map to "omit"
    - Default `<script type=module>` credentials mode to `same-origin`; tested [here](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-script-element/module/resources/credentials-iframe.sub.html)
    - Default `<script type=module>` descendant static `import` credentials mode to `same-origin`; tested [here](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-script-element/module/resources/credentials-iframe.sub.html)
    - Default `<script type=module>` descendant dynamic `import` credentials mode to `same-origin`; tested [here](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-script-element/module/credentials.sub.html) now
    - Default `<link rel=modulepreload>` credentials mode (I guess descendants don't need tested since their fetching in `<link>` context isn't mandatory); ❌not tested, but should probably appear alongside [here](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/preload/modulepreload.html)
 2. Change module worker's default credentials mode to `same-origin` (WorkerOptions)
    - Default credentials mode for top-level module workers to `same-origin`; tested [here](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/workers/modules/dedicated-worker-options-credentials.html)
    - Default credentials mode for module worker descendent imports (static & dynamic) to `same-origin`; ❌not tested, but should probably be included in an extension of the above test
 3. Remove support for cross-origin module workers (by adding a new condition in [fetch a single module script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetch-a-single-module-script) to fetch with `same-origin` request mode. Cross-origin classic workers were not supported before this change)
    - ❌not yet tested; I guess [this test](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/workers/Worker_cross_origin_security_err.htm) should just be extended to include module workers?
 4. Change [default classic script fetch options](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetching-scripts:concept-script-fetch-options-credentials)' credentials mode to `same-origin`
    - Default credentials mode for classic worker dynamic `import`s to `same-origin` ❌not tested, but should maybe be a part of [this test](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/workers/modules/dedicated-worker-options-credentials.html).
    - Default credentials mode for classic worker `importScripts()` to `same-origin` ❌not tested, but should also perhaps be a part of the above test?

Please let me know if I have anything wrong. Seems like the bulk of the testing work has to do with extending the `workers/modules/...credentials` test to include all variations of descendants. If I could get some help with that that would be fantastic.

Aside: Is it a problem that classic worker scripts cannot have third-party descendant imports that require credentials (but I think module workers can)?

Sorry for forgetting about this. So I'm going to push a commit that changes the credentials mode of "default classic script fetch options" to "include". It seems from the standard that would affect classic workers and `javascript:` URLs, both of which seem correct.

I guess classic (normal) scripts are handled differently and haven't been affected by any of the changes.

I haven't done a thorough review of the entire script fetching setup though to ensure I haven't missed anything.

> It seems from the standard that would affect classic workers and javascript: URLs, both of which seem correct.

In particular I am pretty sure it only affects `import()` statements inside those contexts. But yes, we should align all the defaults.

Changes LGTM. Thanks for taking this on.

Wait, no, want to discuss more. So, "default classic script fetch options" affects `import()` statements from classic scripts that don't have the `crossorigin=""` attribute set. So I think it should be `"same-origin"`, not `"include"`. Maybe it is misleadingly-named, although note [the definition](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-script-fetch-options-credentials):

> The credentials mode used for the initial fetch (for module scripts) and for fetching any imported modules (for both module scripts and classic scripts)

---

I wrote up the following commit message on the assumption that it gets changed to `"same-origin"`.

```
* Module scripts are always fetched with request credentials mode
  "same-origin" by default, instead of the previous default of "omit".
  Only worker module scripts can still set that to "omit", using the
  credentials option to the Worker constructor. Non-worker module
  scripts, which only have the crossorigin="" attribute available, can
  only toggle between "same-origin" and "include", similar to how
  crossorigin="" works for other platform features.
* Similarly, import() statements inside of classic scripts now use the
  "same-origin" credentials mode, instead of "omit". This affects both
  <script> elements, where the default can be changed using
  crossorigin="", and other contexts like javascript: URLs and classic
  worker scripts, where the default cannot be changed.
* The top-level script for module workers is always fetched with request
  mode "same-origin". Cross-origin workers did not quite work due to
  service workers.

Fixes #2557. Fixes #3109.

Tests:

* https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/11274
* https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/13176
* https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/issues/13426
```
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1493449 (default credentials handling for module fetches) is fixed for Firefox 64.
Okay, yeah, it seems to only affect `import()` in which case "`same-origin`" is indeed the way to go.
Commit message looks great, thanks for that!
